name: Sun Mengquan
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2019-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun China (2005-2026)
forbes_bio: Sun Mengquan chairs Shandong-based cooking oil company Luhua Group.
Sun began working for the predecessor of Luhua in 1983, when it was a nearly bankrupt metals trading collective with fewer than 10 workers.
Sun shifted the company's business to processing and exporting peanuts, and, later, into peanut oil.

name: Carlie Irsay-Gordon
sec_insider_companies: BlossomHill Therapeutics, Inc. (BLSM) - Director; MBX Biosciences, Inc. (MBX) - Director,TenPercentOwner; Electra Therapeutics, Inc. (ETRA) - Director,TenPercentOwner; Scribe Therapeutics, Inc. (SCTX) - Director; ADARx Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (ADRX) - Director,TenPercentOwner
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Hurun Global (2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Irsay-Gordon is the granddaughter of Robert Irsay, who acquired the Indianapolis Colts in 1972, and the eldest daughter of Jim Irsay, who ran the team from 1997 until his death in May 2025.
She and her sisters, Casey Foyt and Kalen Jackson, inherited what Forbes estimates are equal 33.3% stakes in the franchise. They now rank among the richest female owners in sports.

Irsay-Gordon serves as the Colts' principal owner and CEO. Long seen as her father's likeliest successor, she got early experience leading the franchise when she stepped in for Irsay in 2014 after his legal troubles resulted in a six-game suspension.

Irsay-Gordon once served as a team intern and has been involved with the organization's inner workings for more than two decades, having represented the franchise at NFL owners' meetings as early as 2004. Four years later, she took on a vice president role.
She has demonstrated a hands-on approach, attending meetings with players and coaches and standing on the sideline during games listening to play calls over a headset.

name: Kapil Bhatia
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2016-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun India (2015-2019)
forbes_bio: Kapil Bhatia is the executive chairman of InterGlobe Enterprises, whose biggest asset is a stake in IndiGo, India's largest airline by market share.
IndiGo was set cofounded by his son Rahul Bhatia and started operations in 2006.
IndiGo has a fleet over 350 aircraft and flies to 118 destinations, including 32 overseas.
The other interests of InterGlobe include hospitality, aircraft maintenance and logistics.
Bhatia got his start in the travel business as a sales manager before he set up his own venture called Delhi Express Travels.

name: Paul Fireman
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2007-2025); Hurun Global (2015-2026)
forbes_bio: Paul Fireman bought the US distribution rights for a British company in 1979, turned it into Reebok and rode the sneakers & aerobics craze in the 80s.
Nike pulled ahead in the early 1990s, and shareholders demanded that Fireman step down in 1996, which he eventually did.
Fireman returned in 1999 and revived the business before selling it to Adidas for $3.8 billion in 2005, a deal that earned him $600 million.
Fireman owns Liberty National Golf Course, a $250 million country club built on a New Jersey landfill overlooking the Statue of Liberty.
forbes_facts: Liberty National Golf club is one of the most exclusive courses in the world, with members reportedly paying $500,000 to join.
Before creating Reebok, Fireman was an officer in an outdoor sports distributorship.

name: Mark Dixon
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2017-2026); Sunday Times Rich List (2020)
forbes_bio: Mark Dixon is the founder and executive chairman of IWG (formerly Regus), a flexible workplace provider.
The son of a Ford engineer, Dixon dropped out of school at age 16 to start a business delivering sandwiches by bicycle.
He held jobs as a logger and an encyclopedia salesman before founding IWG in 1989, after spotting businesspeople meeting around coffee tables.
Now the company rents out meeting rooms, office space by the hour, virtual offices and space in co-working sites across more than 120 countries.
forbes_facts: Earlier in his career Dixon launched The Bread Roll Company to supply bread to food vendors after realizing it was hard to procure buns for hot dogs and hamburgers.
Dixon owns the 150-acre Kingscote Estate winery in West Sussex, an area he reportedly hopes will be "a new frontier for wine."

name: Dhruv Sawhney
forbes_bio: Cambridge-educated engineer and Wharton grad, Dhruv Sawhney joined his uncle's floundering engineering and sugar firm and turned it around.
Eventually, he took charge of his father's sugar interests as well and merged the two businesses into Triveni Engineering and Industries.
Triveni produces sugar and liquor and also has a power transmission business. He also owns listed Triveni Turbine, which makes turbines for the power sector.
His older son Tarun runs Triveni Engineering while younger son Nikhil runs Triveni Turbine.
forbes_facts: Chess buff, Sawhney was president of the All India Chess Federation for 12 years.

name: Boris Rotenberg
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2013-2025); Hurun Global (2019-2026)
forbes_bio: Younger brother of Arkady Rotenberg, Boris was his partner in SMP Bank and several infrastructure constrictors.
The Rotenberg brothers were hit by U.S. sanctions and had assets frozen in 2014 because of their close ties to President Vladimir Putin.
The U.S. Treasury claimed that Putin had awarded the Rotenbergs billions of dollars in contracts with Gazprom and for the Sochi Olympics.
Unlike Arkady, Boris was not subject to European Union sanctions because he has Finnish citizenship. The U.K. sanctioned him in February 2022.
In recent years Boris Rotemberg sold almost all of his assets including stake in SMB Bank.
forbes_facts: Boris is vice president of the Russian Judo Federation. He sponsors the SMP Racing Project, which supports young Russian drivers. He also owns Sochi football club.
In 2018 Finnish Defense Forces banned Rotenberg from building a guest house on his site because it is located near a military base.

name: Yoichi Erikawa
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Yoichi Erikawa cofounded videogame developer Koei more than four decades ago with his wife Keiko Erikawa.
The company, now called Koei Tecmo Holdings, trades on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
The founders are stepping away from executive roles. Starting April, Yoichi, who is now CEO, will become chairman; and Keiko, who is now chairman, will become chairman emeritus.
The company is known for its Samurai Warrior games.
Hisashi Koinuma, currently executive vice president, is set to become president and CEO in June.

name: Ben Francis
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2023-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2025); Sunday Times Rich List (2020); Hurun Unicorn founders (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: Ben Francis is the founder and CEO of Solihull, England-based sportswear brand Gymshark.
Francis sold a 21% stake to private equity firm General Atlantic in August 2020, in a deal that valued the company at $1.45 billion; he owns 70%.
He cofounded the company with his friend Lewis Morgan in his parents' garage in 2012 at age 19, when he was still a college student delivering pizzas.
Gymshark grew thanks to partnerships with fitness influencers on social media, paying them small amounts to wear the company's gear in their videos.
The company also has an office in Denver and opened its first brick-and-mortar store on London's Regent Street in October 2022.
forbes_facts: Francis built two fitness apps when he was an 18-year-old college student.
Gymshark started out selling supplements, but Francis and Morgan quickly pivoted to selling fitness gear they made with a screen printer and sewing machine.
